mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned engine replacement for a Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI typically ranges from £2,000 to £3,500 for supply only, depending on the specialist and the extent of upgrades included. Used engines start around £800 but carry higher risk, while rebuilt units include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing 2.0 MPI engine in a Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning signs in the Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI are unexplained coolant loss, white exhaust smoke, or a distinct misfire under load. You should also check for sweet-smelling exhaust, overheating warning lights, or rough idling pointing to distributor cap and rotor arm wear.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a classic Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's overall condition. A typical Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI holds a UK market value of £1,500-£4,000. If the chassis, bodywork and interior are in excellent condition, a £2,000-£3,500 rebuilt engine is a sound investment to preserve a rare classic. If the vehicle is heavily worn, evaluate scrap or part-ex value first.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI typically takes 2 to 4 days, depending on the specialist's workload and whether any ancillary components like the cooling system are being upgraded simultaneously. Sourcing a quality rebuilt unit may add a few days, so always confirm the exact turnaround time with your chosen specialist.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI and the V8 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI uses a 2.0-litre naturally aspirated inline-4 petrol engine (Rover T-series) producing 134 hp, prioritising mechanical simplicity, lighter front-end weight and better fuel economy. In contrast, the 3.9i or 4.0i V8 produces significantly more torque and power but is heavier, thirstier and more complex to maintain.

historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI launched in the mid-1990s, it offered a more affordable, fuel-efficient petrol alternative to the thirsty V8 models, bringing the robust Rover T-series inline-4 to the iconic family 4x4.

milestones.description: Introduction of the 2.0-litre Multi-Point Injection (MPI) petrol engine (134 hp) as an entry-level option for the Discovery Series 1, primarily targeting fleet and specific export markets.
1998 - Continued limited production alongside the 2.5 TDI and V8 variants, before being quietly phased out in favour of the more popular 3.9i and 4.0i V8 petrol engines due to low UK consumer demand.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h3: The 2.0-litre Rover T-series MPI engine in the Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI is mechanically simple and robust, but age-related wear on the cooling system and ignition components is a known pattern. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Head Gasket Failure - Why the Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI 2.0 MPI Overheats
problems.rootCause: Ageing composite head gaskets degrade under sustained thermal cycling, especially if the cooling system has not been regularly flushed, leading to coolant loss, white exhaust smoke and eventual overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace radiator, hoses, thermostat and water pump; flush system and upgrade to modern coolant.
repairOptions.longevity: Extends life significantly if caught before catastrophic overheating damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded head gasket and cooling components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the engine has already suffered thermal damage or a warped cylinder head.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI of relevant age (1994-1998) currently holds a UK market value of approximately £1,500-£4,000 [THIRD-PARTY - Hagerty / Lancaster Insurance classic car valuations], with pristine, low-mileage examples commanding higher premiums. At this value band, a full rebuilt engine replacement may approach or exceed 60% of the vehicle's current market value, making a thorough evaluation of the vehicle's overall condition essential before committing.
problems.recommendation: If your Land Rover Discovery 2.0 MPI is showing minor coolant seepage but has not suffered thermal damage, a comprehensive cooling system refresh by a classic Land Rover specialist is the most cost-effective route. However, if the engine has already overheated and warped the cylinder head, sourcing a low-mileage used or reconditioned unit is often the most financially viable solution for this specific variant.
